Build and tests pass clean. Here's the summary:

## What I found first

The task description said a deterministic codemod had already wrapped some OpenAI/Anthropic client constructions in a `routerRuntime.ts`. That file doesn't exist in this repo — `.router-migrate/apply.json` shows `"edits": [], "runtime_files": []`. The codemod's scanner only recognizes literal `new OpenAI(...)`/`new Anthropic(...)` calls, and this plugin has none: all real traffic goes through LangChain's `ChatOpenAI`/`OpenAI`/`ChatAnthropic` wrapper classes (three dependency layers down) or hand-rolled `fetch()` calls. So I did the full migration from scratch, using the recovered `HANDOFF.md`'s 3 flagged raw-fetch sites as one input, plus my own audit of the LangChain-based providers it couldn't see.

## What I migrated

**`src/router-config.ts`** (new) — reads `RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY`/`RAMP_ROUTER_BASE_URL`, used everywhere else.

**LangChain providers** (`src/LLMProviders/langchain/{base,openaiChat,openaiAgent,chatanthropic}.tsx`):
- Added an opt-in `routerCompatible` flag on the shared base class, set only on `OpenAI Chat`, `OpenAI Agent`, and `Chat Anthropic` — so MiniMax/Perplexity/Together/Mistral/Google/Ollama (which also extend the same base) are untouched.
- When Router is enabled, `configMerger()` swaps `api_key`/`basePath` to Router's, so the user's own OpenAI/Anthropic key is never sent.
- `OpenAI Chat`/`OpenAI Agent` now set `useResponsesApi: true` unconditionally (Chat Completions → Responses, per the task's mapping) and send `reasoning: {effort}` / `maxTokens` as real constructor fields instead of the old `modelKwargs.reasoning_effort` / `bodyParams.max_completion_tokens` hack — the old fields are chat-completions-only and would have 400'd as unknown parameters on `/v1/responses`.
- `Chat Anthropic` needed no schema change (already Messages-shaped); just repoints `anthropicApiUrl`/`anthropicApiKey` to Router, stripping the trailing `/v1` since the Anthropic SDK appends `/v1/messages` itself.

**Raw-fetch "Custom" providers** (`src/LLMProviders/custom/{base,custom,anthropic}.tsx`) — the 3 sites the scanner flagged:
- `Anthropic Legacy (Custom)`: default endpoint/auth now point at Router's `/v1/messages` compat surface with Bearer auth (body/response shape unchanged — already Anthropic Messages format).
- `Default (Custom)`: default endpoint/body/response-parsing rewritten from Chat Completions (`messages`→`choices[0].message`) to Responses (`input`→`output`/`output_text`), including the streaming SSE parser (named `response.output_text.delta` events instead of unnamed chat deltas). These changes only affect the *out-of-the-box default* for a newly added Custom provider — a user who's already repointed `endpoint`/`custom_header`/`custom_body` at their own server (LM Studio, Ollama, etc.) is unaffected, since settings values always win over defaults.

**Verified**: ran a standalone smoke test against the Router simulator — `ChatOpenAI` (plain + `o3-mini` reasoning), and `ChatAnthropic` all produced valid, accepted requests. Full `tsc --noEmit` (85 pre-existing unrelated errors, no new ones), production build, and the 24-test vitest suite all pass with Router both on and off.

## Not migrated

- **`OpenAI Instruct (Langchain)`** (`openaiInstruct.tsx`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`) — uses the legacy `/v1/completions` API, which Router doesn't expose at all, and "instruct" completion-only models generally aren't served through Responses APIs. No safe mapping without guessing.
- **Azure OpenAI / Azure OpenAI Instruct** — these target a user's own Azure resource via deployment-specific addressing, orthogonal to Router's model-id catalog. Redirecting them would hijack a deliberate user choice to use their own Azure deployment.
- **MiniMax, Perplexity, Together, Mistral, Google Gemini/PaLM, Ollama, HuggingFace** — third-party providers with their own protocols/catalogs; task scope was OpenAI/Anthropic traffic specifically, and Router's catalog for these isn'
